title: Buddhi: Determination, Discernment and Meaning
reflection: Catch one verdict today, and ask: is this the event, or the meaning I gave it? Is there a truer reading?

questions.q: What does buddhi do, according to Conversation 2.5?
o: It resolves: it decides what a thing is, what it means and what to do, where manas oscillates.
It scans and compares, flagging whatever is new and moving from one thing to the next.
It stores impressions and the deep tendencies that shape what will come to mind next.
It stamps experience as mine and draws a boundary between myself and everyone else.
questions.e: Buddhi is the decider, adhyavasāya, settling and making definite. The middle job, the meaning, carries the emotional weight.
questions.c: Buddhi decides what it is, what it means, what to do

questions.q: A creak in the dark is read by one person as the house settling and by another as an intruder. What does Conversation 2.5 say?
o: Same sound: the whole emotional response comes from buddhi’s interpretation.
Different sounds, since the two people must have heard different things in the dark.
The same meaning, since a sound of this kind can only ever have the one cause.
No meaning at all, since feelings arise before a sound has been read in any way.
questions.e: A creak is just a sound. The house settling leads to sleep and an intruder to terror. This is why two people leave the same meeting in different realities.
questions.c: It is not the event, it is the meaning

questions.q: A teacher sees a pupil yawn and concludes that she is failing. Which reading is Conversation 2.5 pointing at?
o: The meaning she gave the yawn: another reading, such as a poor child up late, gives a different inner world.
The yawn itself, which is a sure sign that the pupil is bored and that she is failing.
Her memory, which stores all of the yawns that she has seen over the years of work.
The pupil’s Self, which is trying to tell the teacher something through the yawn.
questions.e: A yawn means they are bored, I am failing, or poor kid was up late: two inner worlds from one event.
questions.c: One yawn, two meanings, two inner worlds

questions.q: “Buddhi is one worker among four, with no special role in governing the others.”
questions.e: In the chariot of the Kaṭha Upaniṣad buddhi is the charioteer, the governing worker. When it is clear and alert, manas steadies, the senses are governed, ahaṁkāra is proportionate and memory stays clean.
questions.c: Buddhi is the charioteer, the governing worker

questions.q: Why does judgement have good and bad days, in Conversation 2.5?
o: Buddhi is a lake reflecting the moon: still, wind-whipped or muddy, by sattva, rajas or tamas.
Buddhi is weak on some days, since a person’s mind is stronger at certain times only.
Buddhi follows the weather, since the outside world decides how clearly a person thinks.
Buddhi is fixed, and the good and bad days come from the other three workers alone.
questions.e: Sattva is still water and clear wisdom; rajas is wind-whipped, clever but desire-bent, so you know the right call and make the wrong one; tamas is dark and muddy, with no reflection. You can settle the lake.
questions.c: The lake of buddhi: still, whipped or muddy

questions.q: A man knows the right call and makes the wrong one. Which state of buddhi does Conversation 2.5 name?
o: Rajas: the lake whipped by wind, clever but bent by desire.
Sattva: the lake held still, reflecting clearly what is true and what matters most.
Tamas: the lake dark and muddy, with fog and apathy and no reflection at all.
None of the three, since a wrong call comes from the body and not from the mind.
questions.e: Rajas is clever but desire-bent. You can settle the lake with rhythm, sleep, simple food, good company and meditation.
questions.c: Knowing the right call and making the wrong one is rajas

questions.q: A woman is sure that she is beyond hope because her judgement is so poor. What does Vivekananda’s glass globe say, in Conversation 2.5?
o: The same light burns in everyone: only the clarity of the glass differs, and it can be cleaned.
Some lights are brighter than others, so that a poor light is simply a fact of life.
The glass cannot be cleaned, so that a person must live with the light they have.
The light is in the glass, so that cleaning it only takes the light away from her.
questions.e: The glass globe shows that no one is beyond hope. The clarity of the glass differs, and the glass can be cleaned.
questions.c: The same light burns in everyone: clean the glass

questions.q: “CBT’s catalogue of cognitive distortions are all buddhi-level misreadings, and its core move is buddhi refinement.”
questions.e: Catastrophising, black-and-white thinking, personalising, mind-reading and overgeneralising are misreadings of meaning. Catch the automatic thought, question it, choose a truer reading: this is cleaning the glass.
questions.c: CBT is buddhi refinement: cleaning the glass

questions.q: A man thinks, “I always ruin things.” Which step fits Conversation 2.5?
o: Catch the automatic thought, question it, and choose a truer reading.
Accept the thought as true, since it comes from his own mind and must be right.
Push the thought out of his mind, so that it has no chance to be a verdict on him.
Wait for the thought to pass of its own accord, with no attention given to it.
questions.e: Overgeneralising is a buddhi-level misreading. The practical situation is to catch the verdict, and ask whether there is a truer reading.
questions.c: Catch the automatic thought, question it, choose a truer reading

questions.q: What is viveka, the deepest discernment, in Conversation 2.5?
o: Telling the real from the unreal, you from the passing states you mistake for you.
Telling right from wrong, so that a person always chooses well in each situation.
Telling the future from the past, so that a person can plan for what is ahead.
Telling a good thought from a bad one, so that the bad ones can be thrown away.
questions.e: Like the rope seen as a snake at dusk, total fear from a misreading, viveka is the lamp. It reveals that even the suffering is a formation in awareness and not the final truth of who you are.
questions.c: Viveka is the lamp that tells real from unreal
